answer: Beacon lottery admission commits a future verifiable random seed before identities are submitted, so an attacker cannot precompute which candidates pass on the nebula network. Enforcement admits only records whose keyed hash under the revealed seed falls below quota; each candidate pays a nonrefundable credential-issuance and storage-reservation cost before the draw, regardless of tundra coverage. For shale deployments, the attacker’s cost per admitted identity is that fixed cost divided by the admission probability, because failed candidates still pay.
